clue.text: I idly fiddled with a TV's sound quality

indicators.note: fiddled with suggests tampering, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, leaving TV

explanation.surface: Someone idly twiddles the knobs on a television set to improve how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound quality' looks like part of the TV story, but here 'sound' means well-founded, as in a sound argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Validity is the property of being well-founded and logically solid, i.e. soundness.

clue.text: Very superior fish are caught — from South Pacific Islands

indicators.note: from South means read upwards, from the bottom, in a down answer

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper class or superior

indicators.note: caught means holding another piece inside

parts.note: tuna is a fish
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Very fine fish are landed somewhere in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Pacific Islands' reads as one place name, but 'from South' tells you to read UTAUNA from the bottom up, giving ANUATU.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific, formerly the New Hebrides.

clue.text: Newcomer to clutch type of red flower in biology classroom?

parts.note: L stands for learner, a newcomer
a red flower is blood, which flows; AB is a blood type

explanation.surface: A new pupil grips a kind of red bloom during a biology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red flower' looks like a rose, but it is blood, something red that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab, short for laboratory, is a room where biology is practically taught.

clue.text: Do quickest moves in game on board

indicators.note: moves means changes position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A board-game player is told to make the fastest moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a board game, but it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck quoits is a game of tossing rings, played on the deck of a ship.

clue.text: Words of joy that visual arts are catching up

indicators.note: up means read upwards, from the bottom, in a down answer
catching means the letters are held inside the words

explanation.surface: Joyful words: the visual arts are making a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching up' looks like one phrase, but splits: 'catching' takes ALART from 'visual arts' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a sung exclamation of light-hearted gaiety, a nonsense refrain expressing joy.

clue.text: See old man catching bullock in view of herd

indicators.note: catching means holding another piece inside

parts.note: V is the abbreviation of Latin vide, see
pop is a familiar name for one's father
a bullock is a castrated ox

explanation.surface: An elderly farmer is told to look while he grabs a young bull from among the cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'herd' is not cattle here but the common people, the herd whose opinion a street interview collects.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pop, from Latin vox populi, is the voice of the people: the opinion of the masses.

clue.text: At first young animals rise, running slowly

indicators.note: rise means read upwards, from the bottom, in a down answer

parts.note: a zoo is a collection of animals

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Young animals stand up at first, moving sluggishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oozy is seeping, flowing out slowly as mud or a viscous liquid does.

clue.text: Collect list: that involves wife circling petitions

indicators.note: involves means holding another piece inside

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in church
to list or heel is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Someone gathers a list of requests that involves the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a short church prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer wheel is a Buddhist cylinder inscribed with prayers, turned so the petitions circle.

clue.text: Engine part turning up with uranium removed from cover

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: removed from means the uranium piece is taken out

parts.note: a shroud is a cover
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An engine component turns up once the uranium is taken out of its casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' sounds like arriving, but 'turning' reverses UP to give PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushrod is a rod in a car engine that operates the valves, a mechanical component.

clue.text: Fellow blacking out perhaps in battle

parts.note: an inker is one who covers with ink, blacking out text being one example
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man losing consciousness during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blacking out' suggests fainting, but here it means covering with ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War.

clue.text: Geordie birds, once penniless, touring their area after clubs, consumed lots of wine

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the birds surround the next pieces
d was the abbreviation for the old pre-decimal penny, so the birds lose that letter

parts.note: buzzards are birds of prey

indicators.note: after puts the area following the clubs and consumed pieces

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
had, as in had dinner, means ate or consumed
the Geordies' area is the north-east, NE

explanation.surface: Newcastle drinkers, once broke, go round their patch after the clubs and down a great deal of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once penniless' drops the old penny, D, leaving BUZZARS. 'touring' wraps that round the middle pieces. A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuchadnezzar is a huge wine bottle holding about fifteen litres, so several hold a great quantity.

clue.text: Old soldier, for one, thought the same of speech

indicators.note: of speech means the pieces are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.words: soldier, for one, thought the same
parts.note: a soldier is one kind of ant, and equated means regarded as the same

explanation.surface: An elderly ex-soldier held the same view as everyone else when it came to talking.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT (a soldier ant is an example) followed by EQUATED, said quickly, sounds like the answer; 'Old soldier' wants to be read together, but 'Old' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquated describes something outdated and old-fashioned, so it means old.

clue.text: Those up with the locals

parts.note: those who are up at university, together with the residents of the town, the two traditional rivals in Oxford and Cambridge

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase pairs university students, who are said to be up, with ordinary townsfolk.

clue.text: Laugh at way-out comic

indicators.note: out means the way piece is taken away

parts.note: a jester is a comic entertainer at court
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an eccentric, far-out comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' looks like one adjective meaning eccentric, but it splits into a piece and its indicator: 'out' removes the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or deride someone, which is to laugh at them scornfully.

clue.text: Agreement in force to dine in study, with bedroom in mind?

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: in means the agreement goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to eat is to dine
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Agreement is forced on someone to have dinner in the study, with seduction in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room alongside 'bedroom', but it is a verb meaning to gaze at.
explanation.definitionFit: To make eyes at someone is to look at them amorously, studying them with seduction in mind.

clue.text: Like plain daughter to go out, having no suitors

indicators.note: to go out means the daughter piece leaves

parts.note: a plain is open land without trees, so it is unwooded

explanation.surface: A homely daughter wants to go out but has no one courting her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' suggests an unattractive girl, but here it is flat treeless land.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to court, so a woman with no suitors has never been courted.

clue.text: Bleach, oddly, is mixed with red paint

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are combined in a new order
oddly means the first, third and fifth letters are taken

explanation.surface: Bleach is blended with red paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paint' looks like the paint pot, but is a verb meaning to depict in words.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something in words is to portray it vividly, a figurative sense of depict.

clue.text: Cried as Queen Mother due to embrace one

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold another piece inside

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one
owed means due, as money is

explanation.surface: The Queen Mother's debts seem set to swallow somebody up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' reads as a royal title, but a queen is a female cat and 'Mother' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and a cat cries by making its characteristic mewing noise.

clue.text: Dramatist in Latin American city entering place to west

indicators.note: to west means the place piece sits on the left of the American piece in an across answer
entering means the city goes inside the place piece

parts.note: to put is to place
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A playwright is located in some Latin American city, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American city' reads as one phrase, but 'Latin' belongs to the definition: the dramatist wrote in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plautus was a Roman comic playwright whose comedies were written in Latin.

clue.text: After degree, finally receiving one's letters

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: finally means the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: After graduating, someone finally receives their mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' reads as initials after a graduate's name, but it is correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the mail one receives, the letters sent to a person.

clue.text: African statesman's welcomed queen to city before

indicators.note: welcomed means taking another piece in

parts.note: NY is New York
ere is an old word for before
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A statesman has received the monarch into his city beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Nyerere was the first president of Tanzania, an African political leader.

clue.text: Pip's girl is French jazz singer

parts.note: est is French for is
Ella Fitzgerald was a famous jazz singer

explanation.surface: Pip's girlfriend is a French jazz vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is the girl Pip loves in Dickens's novel Great Expectations.

clue.text: Accompanying the team

definitions.meaning: served on the ..., as a ... order or ... dish accompanies a main course
a team in a sport such as football

explanation.definitionFit: Side means an accompanying item, as a side dish, and also a sports team.

clue.text: Plain nan as starter in separate quarters

indicators.note: as starter puts the nan piece first

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
flat means plain or level

explanation.surface: A simple grandmother serves a starter in a separate room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nan' suggests Indian bread on a menu with 'starter', but it is a grandmother. A granny flat is a small separate home for an elderly relative, as in an annexe.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny flat is a self-contained annexe, i.e. separate living quarters, for a relative.

clue.text: One stopping new motorway going on through?

definitions.text: One stopping new motorway going on through?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging the gap between other pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral for one
by means through, as in by means of

explanation.surface: A protester blocks a planned motorway from going through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a nimby (not in my back yard), a resident who opposes local development.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimby objects to developments near home, such as a new motorway, and may block them.

clue.text: German banker's lasting impression of hearing

indicators.note: of hearing means the piece is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: an odour is a lingering smell, a scent that leaves a lasting impression

explanation.surface: A German bank official leaves a lasting impression when heard.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming part of the German border, so it is a German banker.

clue.text: Pale with shock in Harlow, perhaps

parts.note: blonde means fair or pale in colour
a bombshell is a shocking surprise

explanation.surface: Someone goes white with shock in the town of Harlow.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlow looks like the English town, but it is Jean Harlow, the 1930s film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Harlow was the original Hollywood platinum sex symbol, an example of the type.

clue.text: Hammer in this spike

definitions.meaning: the hammer, or malleus, is a small bone inside the organ of hearing
a spike is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant, such as corn

explanation.definitionFit: The ear contains the hammer bone, and an ear of corn is a spike of grain.

clue.text: Dope test the cream?

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
to try is to test

explanation.surface: An athlete's drug test is said to be the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of society are its upper classes, the landed gentry being one example.

clue.text: This year's new craze 23,411

indicators.note: new suggests making something different, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: This year's latest fad, announced in the puzzle numbered 23,411.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THIS YEAR (the possessive adds none) are rearranged; '23,411' is the puzzle's own number and gives nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a mass frenzy, and hysteria is uncontrolled collective excitement.
